items.title: The Soviet Union dissolved on 26 December 1991

options.text: After Gorbachev's perestroika and glasnost reforms, the August 1991 hardline coup failed, Baltic states declared independence, Yeltsin took power in Russia; the USSR was formally dissolved by the Belavezha Accords (8 December) and Gorbachev's resignation (25 December); the Supreme Soviet voted itself out of existence on 26 December 1991
By a vote of all citizens in 1989

items.reveal:
Mikhail Gorbachev became General Secretary in March 1985. Perestroika (restructuring) and glasnost (openness) loosened Soviet controls. Eastern European communism collapsed in 1989. The Baltic states declared independence in 1990-91.

The August 1991 coup by hardliners against Gorbachev failed within three days when Boris Yeltsin rallied resistance from a tank outside the Russian White House. Real power shifted from the USSR to Russia.

The Belavezha Accords (8 December 1991) saw the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus declare the USSR dissolved. The Alma-Ata Protocol (21 December) added eight more republics. Gorbachev resigned on 25 December; the Supreme Soviet voted on 26 December.
items.why: The largest peaceful end of a superpower in history. The mechanism — internal reform, failed counter-coup, voluntary dissolution by republics — has shaped how subsequent transitions have been imagined.

items.title: The Royal Society was founded in 1660 with a royal charter from Charles II
items.claim: What is the Royal Society and when was it founded?

options.text: A learned society for natural philosophy founded 28 November 1660, granted royal charters by Charles II in 1662 and 1663, with the motto 'Nullius in verba' ('take nobody's word for it')
A department of the College of Arms

items.reveal:
Twelve men met at Gresham College, London, on 28 November 1660 after a lecture by Christopher Wren, to form 'a Colledge for the Promoting of Physico-Mathematicall Experimentall Learning'. Early members included Robert Boyle, Robert Hooke (curator of experiments), John Wilkins and Wren.

The motto 'Nullius in verba' (taken from Horace) signalled commitment to experiment over authority. The Philosophical Transactions, first published in 1665, is the world's oldest continuously published scientific journal.

Isaac Newton served as President from 1703 until his death in 1727. Charles II reportedly mocked the society for 'weighing air'.
items.why: Modern science as an institutional practice has a specific founding moment. The 1660 Restoration created intellectual breathing space for a society that has shaped global science ever since.

items.title: Eratosthenes calculated Earth's circumference within 1-15%
items.claim: Around 240 BCE, Eratosthenes of Cyrene calculated Earth's circumference using shadows. How accurate was he?

options.text: Off by an order of magnitude
His value (around 250,000 stadia) is, depending on which stadion he used, within 1-15% of the modern value of ~40,075 km
His method was sound but he had no actual figure
He was the first to argue Earth was flat

items.reveal_title: Two sticks and a hired pacer
items.reveal:
Eratosthenes knew the sun shone straight down a well at Syene (Aswan) at noon on the summer solstice. At Alexandria, a vertical stick cast a shadow at the same moment, with an angle of about 1/50 of a circle (7.2°). He paid a 'bematist' (professional pacer) to measure the distance — about 5,000 stadia.

50 × 5,000 = 250,000 stadia. The exact length of a stadion is uncertain (157 m to 185 m), giving a circumference between ~39,000 km and ~46,000 km. The true value is 40,075 km at the equator.
items.why: The 'ancients thought Earth was flat' myth is wrong about both the ancients and the science. Greek geometry was capable of measuring planetary dimensions to within a few percent over 2,200 years ago.
